title: Worked Examples Moderate the Effect of Math Learning Anxiety on Children's Math Learning and Engagement During the COVID-19 Pandemic
author: Barton, Craig
source: Tips for Teachers (tipsforteachers.co.uk), December 18, 2024 — original paper: https://www.r
summary: Barton's page covers a study by Mesingha and colleagues testing whether worked examples moderate the impact of math anxiety and pandemic-related worry on fifth-grade students' learning and engagement. Across a two-day, 280-student lesson on ratio, math anxiety negatively predicted learning outcomes, but students who worked through worked examples had those negative effects mitigated, particularly for procedural and conceptual understanding and engagement. Pandemic-related worries did not directly harm learning but did affect affective and motivational outcomes. Notably, the protective benefit of worked examples did not show up on an immediate post-test but only emerged three days later, suggesting the effect operates on consolidation rather than immediate performance. The intervention itself was simple: screenshots of the teacher's worked solution strategy inserted at key points in an otherwise ordinary video lesson. Barton frames this as a low-cost, easily implementable way to support anxious or worried learners without redesigning an entire unit.
points: Worked examples reduce cognitive load and specifically buffer students with higher math anxiety from its negative effects on learning and engagement.
The benefit of worked examples shows up in both procedural and conceptual understanding of the target concept (ratio), not just mechanical accuracy.
The protective effect of worked examples was delayed, appearing on a three-day-later post-test rather than immediately, so short-term data may understate the benefit.
The intervention was minimal effort: screenshots of a teacher's worked solution inserted into an existing video lesson at key points.
